correctness.rationale: Original proof contains a FALSE claim that when 7 divides both U=108m²+1 and V=27m²+16, its exponents in both are exactly one. Counterexamples: m=11 gives exponents (1,2) and m=17 gives (4,1). The theorem itself survives after corrected full proof: U−4V=−63 gives min(v7(U),v7(V))=1, not both equal one; the two U linear roots and one V root are pairwise distinct mod7 from triple gcd one. If one exponent >1, its 1 or 2 disjoint maximal-valuation roots cannot be invariant under 7^(max−1), forcing full higher 7-power period. Other odd primes and 2 cases follow prime-wise valuation roots. Reconstructed all polynomial identities, triple gcd, CRT-free per-prime lower bound and full local-period argument from corrected final RESULT.md. 9000 exact direct quotient comparisons and all 4 high-7-power regression cases passed corrected verify.py.
